decision_conditions: <p>In the absence of a completed legal agreement to secure a financial contribution equivalent to 20% affordable housing provision, the proposal fails to demonstrate compliance with Merton Local Plan (2024) policy H11.1(f), which requires schemes of 2–9 homes to provide a cash-in-lieu contribution equivalent to 20% affordable housing (split 70% low-cost rent / 30% intermediate, including a minimum of 25% First Homes).</p><div><br></div>

<p>The first floor unit, with a GIA of 68.5sqm, would fall short of the minimum 70sqm standard required for a 2-bedroom, 4-person dwelling, resulting in a substandard living environment for future occupiers, contrary to London Plan (2021) policy D6 (Housing quality and standards) and Merton Local Plan (2024) policy D12.3 (Ensuring high quality design for all developments).</p>

<p>The proposal would result in the loss of a family-sized (3-bed) dwelling without the re-provision of an equivalent family-sized unit, contrary to Merton Local Plan (2024) policies H11.1(c) (Housing choice) and D12.10(2) (Dwelling Conversions), which require conversions of existing family-sized homes into two or more smaller units to re-provide at least one family-sized (3-bed or more) home.</p>

<p>By reason of its excessive depth, bulk and flat roof design, the proposed rear extension would result in an overly bulky and unsightly addition, harmful to the character and appearance of the host dwelling and surrounding area, contrary to National Decision Making Policy DP3 (Key principles for well-designed places) of the National Planning Policy Framework 2026, London Plan (2021) policy D4 (Delivering good design), and Merton Local Plan (2024) policies D12.3 (Ensuring high quality design for all developments) and D12.4 (Alterations and extensions to existing buildings).</p>

<p>By reason of its excessive scale, form, massing and siting, the proposed rear extension would result in an unacceptable sense of enclosure and would be overbearing towards the ground floor flat at no. 21 Grand Drive, causing material harm to the outlook and living conditions of its occupiers, contrary to National Decision Making Policy P3 (Living conditions and pollution) of the National Planning Policy Framework 2026 and Merton Local Plan (2024) policy D12.3(g).</p>

<p>In the absence of any measures to improve the energy performance of the existing dwelling, the proposal fails to demonstrate that greenhouse gas emissions have been minimised on site, contrary to Merton Local Plan (2024) policy CC2.2 (Minimising Greenhouse Gas Emissions).</p>

SINGLE DWELLINGHOUSE INTO TWO FLATS, AND ANCILLARY WORKS.
